transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2026-08-26 16:00 PT
- Duration: 48 minutes (scheduled 45)
- Attendees: Samira (AE), Ethan (SE), Maya (CSM) - Redwood; Jordan (CTO), Priya (Platform Eng), Leo (Head of AI), Ava (Security) - Copper Arch

Summary (auto): Quick standup to confirm commitments for the Dedicated pilot and to clear up network/KMS questions. Agreed next steps around benchmarking and SOW.

[00:00] Samira: All right, everyone, thanks for making time, appreciate it. quick call, standup / commitment review for the pilot. umm, we'll run through timeline, network, security, and then next steps.
[00:27] Jordan: Yep thanks. we've got three folks on from infra, plus me. primary goal is to validate latency targets and make sure we can meet the SLA for our customer-facing assistant.
[00:40] Ethan: Great, can you remind us the latency p95 target you care about and the qps burst profile? I have a note from the intake but want to confirm.
[00:52] Priya: We're seeing about 60 qps average, spikes to 180 qps during business hours, target p95 is about 250ms for short prompts (<128 tokens) but we can tolerate 400ms if cost delta is huge.
[01:08] Leo: yes that's right - p95 250ms is ideal. want to avoid meaningfully higher.
[01:14] Maya: Just to note, part of success will be token cost per 1k and also fallbacks. we want graceful degradation if Dedicated pool saturates.

[01:32] Ethan: On the Dedicated sizing, recommended starting point is a 4-GPU pool with autoscale bump to 6 for bursts, depends on model variant. We have a suggested config in the doc I sent - the kernel selection and batching heuristics matter a lot for those numbers.
[01:48] Priya: when you say 4-GPU, is that A100, H100, or are we flexible?
[01:53] Ethan: We usually benchmark on A100s for parity but can recommend H100 if you want better latency for the same token throughput. our Dedicated pricing will reflect that.
[02:02] Jordan: cost matters; we need to compare hosted vs dedicated delta. can you give an example per-1k token cost?
[02:09] Samira: We'll send a detailed pricing sheet as part of the pilot SOW, but rough delta is about 40-55% improvement in unit cost on Dedicated compared to hosted for steady state workloads, depending on batching and KV cache hit rate.
[02:28] Priya: KV cache — small nit, you mentioned KV cache and prefix caching in the doc; how does that work with our multi-tenant prompt routing? any risk of leakage across customers?
[02:40] Ethan: Good question. Redwood's runtime isolates KV cache per-tenant by default; there's a strict namespace separation. there have been edge cases in community docs where transcriptions said 'KV' spelled K-V, etc. but for you, we can show the config.
[02:58] Ava: On the security front, we need specifics: SOC2 scope, audit logs, SSO integration, and KMS (we use CloudKMS with customer-managed keys). can Redwood support CMEK + HSM-backed keys?
[03:14] Samira: Yes, we support CMEK and can integrate with customer-managed KMS providers. for HSM specifics we'll need to confirm compatibility matrix, but we do integrate with common providers. I'll attach our security packet after this meeting.

[03:34] Jordan: Also data residency: our EU customers must have inference in eu-west-1. Does Dedicated let us pin region?
[03:42] Ethan: Dedicated pools can be regional and we support pinning. for the pilot we'll propose a US-west pool, but production you can request eu-west.

[04:00] Speaker 1: (mumble) earlier doc had some mention of private link vs peering, which do you recommend?
[04:08] Priya: yes network question - we prefer PrivateLink if possible because of routing controls, but peering is okay for internal teams.
[04:16] Ethan: Both are supported. PrivateLink is easier for strict network isolation and avoids routing table changes; peering is lower latency lower cost sometimes. We'll list pros/cons in the SOW.

[04:35] Maya: quick ops question — who will be our day-zero contact for incidents during the pilot?
[04:40] Samira: For the pilot you'll have a dedicated CSM (that's me + Maya) and on-call SE rotation. Ethan will be primary SE for the first week of benchmarks.

[05:00] Leo: benchmark plan? what exactly will you run?
[05:04] Ethan: We'll run a micro-benchmark: your sample prompt set (you provide) across target seq lengths, measure p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput and token cost. We'll run with and without prefix/KV caching and with batching tuned.
[05:19] Priya: sample prompts — we'll send a set of 25 typical prompts plus a spike script. format as CSV?
[05:25] Ethan: CSV or JSON lines is fine. include expected tokens and a label for prompt type.

[05:38] Jordan: timeline — we want pilot in Sept; suggested go/no-go by mid-Sept. Can Redwood commit?
[05:45] Samira: Yes, we can target pilot start first week of Sept. SOW draft out by Fri (Aug 28) — does that timeline work?
[05:55] Priya: makes sense, we'll review and get back.

[06:02] Ava: compliance Q — do you keep raw transcripts? retention policy?
[06:07] Ethan: We can configure retention and redaction. default logs for Hosted include request metadata; for Dedicated we give options to keep logs off or forward to your SIEM. we'll outline options.

[06:25] Speaker 1: there was a note about rollouts and fallback model variants in the doc, can you explain quickly?
[06:33] Ethan: Sure — the runtime supports policy-based routing: if Dedicated pool is saturated, requests can fall back to a cheaper hosted variant or to a quantized model. We can set per-route fallbacks and SLOs. this helps keep the UI responsive at cost.
[06:53] Jordan: what's the expected degradation in quality with the quantized variant?
[06:58] Leo: depends on model and prompts; we can do small evals. part of Redwood Optimize is model/quant recommendations — we'll include a quality monitoring reg alert tied to prompt sets.

[07:15] Samira: Ok, let's switch to concrete SOW items — deliverables will be: SOW doc, pricing sheet, benchmark runbook, security packet, and a 45m security deep-dive meeting.
[07:30] Maya: I'll coordinate the security meeting; any preferred times?
[07:34] Ava: afternoons PT work better.

[07:40] Ethan: For the benchmark, could Priya share sample load pattern? spike and baseline? we'll need the realistic traffic to simulate burst behavior.
[07:49] Priya: yes, I'll attach a k6 script and sample CloudWatch graphs.

[08:02] Jordan: On contract terms, we'd like a 3-month pilot with SLA targets and option to convert to annual reserved capacity. Any blockers?
[08:10] Samira: Not from our side; we'll include conversion options and conversion credit in SOW.

[08:18] Speaker 1: (overlap) about telemetry — can we get token-level breakdowns per-route?
[08:23] Ethan: yes, Redwood Console provides per-route token cost breakdowns and traces. we'll demo that in the runbook.

[08:36] Priya: any notes on rolling updates to models? we need canary and rollback.
[08:41] Ethan: Rollouts support canary and A/B; we also have automatic fallback policies. we can show the console route for that.

[09:00] Jordan: would like to see a proof that private deployment won't leak logs to your hosted control plane — we need an architecture diagram.
[09:08] Samira: we'll include a network/architecture diagram in the security packet; for Private control plane options we'll clarify where metadata flows.

[09:22] Leo: small nit: in your benchmarks please include sequence length distributions - we have a lot of mid-length (~256) contexts.
[09:30] Ethan: noted. we'll include 64/128/256+ buckets.

[09:38] Maya: logistics — I'll set up two calendar invites: bench kickoff (30m) and security deep-dive (45m).

[09:46] (brief mute while documents are shared)

[10:05] Samira: quick check on responsibilities - I will send SOW + pricing, Ethan will run micro-benchmark, Priya to provide prompts and load profile, Ava to confirm KMS provider, Jordan to sign off on pilot scope. we have owners for all main items.

[10:25] Priya: we'll also ask infra to validate peering options; might prefer PrivateLink so we'll confirm in doc.

[10:30] Jordan: thanks everyone, this was concise. any open questions?
[10:34] Ethan: just one last note on logging — if you want audit logs to be forwarded to your SIEM, we need an endpoint and retention policy.
[10:42] Ava: we'll provide SIEM endpoint after security meeting.

Recap (auto):
- Redwood deliverables: SOW + pricing (Samira) by Fri Aug 28, benchmark runbook and bench run (Ethan) next Tue, security packet and arch diagram attached to SOW, schedule security deep-dive (Maya).
- Customer deliverables: sample prompts + load script (Priya) by Mon Aug 31, KMS confirmation (Ava) by Sep 4, pilot scope signoff (Jordan) mid-Sep.

Links referenced: SOW draft (link: https://app.redwood/sow-drafts/CA-8742 - placeholder), security packet (will attach), benchmark template (link: internal drive - benchmark-template.csv).

End of transcript.
